document.abstract: Well before the war of 1939–1945 the Laboratoire Central de l'Armement, with Engineer-General Libessart, was already interested in techniques for ultra-high-speed photography and cinematography. In 1946, after an interruption of several years, a new team was put on this subject. The period from 1946 to 1954 was utilized to train engineers and technicians in these very special techniques, mainly in the area of study rather than of practice. The Paris Congress of 1954 marked the end of this period of adaptation, and the new orientation was toward the following objectives: Research on the limits of precision of different types of existing equipment, the development of new n-struments and the establishment of new processes for industrial requirements which would lead to very reliable equipment of high performance and simple operation. The trends and accomplishments in the following two fields are reviewed: Photography and cinematography by transparence and reflection of nonluminous objects, and the photography and cinematography of self-luminous objects.
